ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-filing screening of all directors, officers, shareholders, and 25%+ UBOs against FINTRAC record-making requirements under PCMLTFA; UN Security Council Consolidated List; US OFAC SDN List; Canada's Criminal Code Part II.1 listed entities; Global Affairs Canada sanctions schedules under the Special Economic Measures Act (including Russia, Iran, Venezuela); and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act. AGLC adds a 'fit and proper person' assessment covering integrity, solvency, criminal history, and adverse media; FINTRAC-compliant Politically Exposed Person (PEP) and Heads of International Organizations checks for both domestic and foreign PEPs as defined in SOR/2002-184.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry, operated by Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction; online NUANS pre-clearance via authorized corporate registry service providers linked to the Registrar of Companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use the English and/or French alphabet (Roman script) with Arabic numerals; accents are permitted in French forms; non-Latin scripts (CJK, Cyrillic, etc.) must be transliterated into English or French; the name must end with the prescribed ULC legal element ('Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC') as required under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the Registrar issues written grounds; the applicant may (i) file a revised NUANS report and amended articles within 5 business days, which effectively opens a fresh 90-day reservation window, or (ii) within 30 calendar days of the written refusal, apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the appeal rights in ABCA s 15 et seq. for an order directing approval; submissions are typically written only, with no oral hearing; AGLC name-consent letters may cure liquor-sector sensitive references.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permitted for the statutory registered office only where a licensed Alberta corporate services provider maintains a physical street address and accepts legal service during business hours; a P.O. Box is prohibited. However, the AGLC wholesale liquor licence requires a separate physical cold-chain keg storage facility in Alberta; thus a purely virtual substance model will not satisfy AGLC premise and fit-and-proper requirements for the operating licence.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 70% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within 12 months of AGLC licence issuance; 90% within 24 months, driven by AGLC premise audits, CBSA excise and customs inspections, municipal fire code checks, and cold-chain food-safety verification.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c B-9, including sections 6-11 on incorporation and articles, section 15 on shareholder liability where articles provide for unlimited liability, sections 102-117 on directors and officers, and sections 118-125 on corporate records and registers. The Business Corporations Regulation and Alberta corporate registry filing rules also apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta and Red Tape Reduction
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation, Alberta Business Corporations Act Form 1, filed through an authorized Alberta registry agent or approved electronic registry channel
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies. Shares may be issued for consideration determined by the directors, subject to the articles and the Alberta Business Corporations Act. No statutory escrow account is required. The corporation must record issued shares, consideration received, shareholders, and stated capital in its securities and corporate records. For an Alberta unlimited liability corporation, the articles must expressly provide for unlimited shareholder liability.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the corporation accept and record the subscription by [Subscriber] for [number and class] shares for consideration of CAD [amount], payable as stated in the subscription agreement; that the registered office and records office be established at [Alberta address]; that [Name] be appointed director and [Names] be appointed President, Secretary, Treasurer, and other required officers, subject to the articles and bylaws; that the corporate bank account be opened with [Bank]; and that any director or officer be authorized to complete filings, execute licences, and take all actions necessary to commence lawful operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Confirm Name and Unlimited Liability Structure
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a numbered corporation or reserve a distinctive corporate name. Obtain an Alberta NUANS report where a named corporation is proposed. Confirm that the articles expressly state unlimited liability and that the proposed business, share structure, registered office, and records office comply with the Alberta Business Corporations Act.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name or numbered corporation request
Alberta NUANS name search report, if applicable
Share structure and share rights schedule
Registered office and records office details
Beneficial ownership and identity information required by the registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended name or incorporate under a numbered name. If the ULC wording is omitted, file articles of amendment before issuing shares or commencing operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and Execute Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry filing window or authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 with the corporation name, registered office, share classes, restrictions, number and address of directors, and any unlimited-liability provision. Execute the articles and supporting declarations in the manner accepted by the registry agent. Notarization is generally not required for routine electronic incorporation, but foreign execution, certified copies, or registry-specific affidavits must be notarized where requested.
required_dossiers: Certified translations for documents not in English
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct rejected fields, inconsistent names, director information, or share provisions and resubmit through the same registry channel. Obtain a written registry clarification where the rejection concerns ULC liability language.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pay Fees and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry and authorized registry agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Pay the applicable Alberta government incorporation fee and registry-agent service fee. The base Alberta government incorporation fee is generally CAD 275, exclusive of name-search and agent charges; the USD figure is an approximate conversion and must be verified on the filing date. Obtain the Certificate of Incorporation, filed articles, corporation number, and Alberta registration records.
required_dossiers: Corporate access number and registry receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment or issuance fails, obtain the registry transaction reference, correct payment or identity issues, and request reprocessing. If the registry identifies a substantive defect, file corrected articles or an amendment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation; Alberta Corporate Registry for subsequent statutory filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the organizational meeting or execute unanimous written resolutions. Adopt bylaws, appoint directors and officers, approve the registered and records offices, authorize banking, approve the business plan and licensing applications, accept share subscriptions, issue shares for documented consideration, and update the securities register, register of directors, minute book, and beneficial ownership records.
required_dossiers: Share certificates or electronic ownership records
Registered office and records office records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify defective resolutions by replacement written resolutions, ratification, or a properly convened meeting. Correct the corporate register immediately and preserve an audit trail of all corrections.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete Federal Tax and Excise Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency, including the CRA Business Registration Online service and Excise Compliance Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Business Number and register for GST/HST as required. Register payroll accounts if employees will be engaged. Before manufacturing or packaging beer in Canada, apply for the applicable CRA excise licence under the Excise Act, 2001, maintain premises and production records, and implement duty reporting and payment controls.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and corporate number
Excise licence application and premises plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to CRA information requests within the stated deadline, provide premises or ownership evidence, and request reconsideration or correction through the assigned CRA officer. Do not manufacture or package excisable beer before required authorization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Alberta Liquor Manufacturing and Distribution Authorizations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission, Liquor Licensing and Compliance Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the Alberta manufacturer licence applicable to beer production and any separate authorizations required for on-site sales, taproom service, warehousing, agency arrangements, or wholesale distribution. Submit ownership, premises, floor plans, municipal approvals, CRA excise information, product details, and responsible-management documentation. Obtain written authorization before manufacturing, selling, or distributing liquor.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and corporate ownership chart
Lease or proof of premises control
CRA excise licence or application evidence
Product, packaging, storage, and distribution procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure deficiencies identified by AGLC, provide supplemental ownership or premises records, and request reconsideration or an administrative review where an application is refused or conditions are disputed. No unlicensed liquor activity should continue during review.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Applicable Alberta municipality, including planning, development, building, fire, business-licensing, and utility departments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm zoning permits brewery manufacturing, cold storage, wholesale distribution, loading, alcohol service, and truck access. Obtain development, building, plumbing, electrical, occupancy, business, signage, and fire approvals as applicable. Arrange inspections before occupancy and before commissioning production equipment.
required_dossiers: Electrical, plumbing, mechanical, and drainage plans
Lease, site plan, and utility capacity evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to municipal plan-review comments, revise drawings, obtain variances where legally available, and request inspection rebooking after deficiencies are corrected. Do not occupy or operate in breach of zoning or building conditions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Implement Occupational Health, Food, and Product Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Occupational Health and Safety, Alberta Health Services, Canadian Food Inspection Agency, and applicable municipal health authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for workers compensation where required, implement Alberta OHS procedures, WHMIS training, confined-space and chemical controls, and incident reporting. Confirm food and beverage sanitation requirements, potable-water controls, packaging and labelling compliance, allergen information, and traceability. Ensure beer labels and advertising comply with federal and Alberta requirements.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inspection findings within the prescribed period, submit evidence of remediation, and request a follow-up inspection. Withdraw or correct non-compliant labels and products where required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis Commission for liquor manufacturing and distribution licensing; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas for environmental approvals; the applicable municipality for land-use, building, fire, occupancy, and business approvals; Canada Revenue Agency for federal beer excise authorization.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: AGLC Manufacturer Licence for beer, supplemented by the CRA federal excise licence under the Excise Act, 2001 and any applicable AGLC wholesale, retail, taproom, or delivery authorization

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Generally no standalone full Environmental Impact Assessment for a small existing-site microbrewery; project-specific review and approvals remain required under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, including wastewater, air, hazardous materials, waste, and water-use requirements. A full assessment may be triggered by project scale, site sensitivity, or a designated activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Obtain municipal wastewater-connection or industrial-discharge approval before discharging brewery effluent. Meet applicable municipal sewer bylaws and approval limits for pH, biochemical oxygen demand, chemical oxygen demand, total suspended solids, temperature, fats, oils, grease, nutrients, and flow. Do not discharge untreated high-strength wort, yeast, chemicals, or cleaning solutions. Control boiler and process emissions under applicable Alberta air requirements, maintain VOC and chemical inventories, and segregate, label, store, transport, and document spent chemicals, fuel, packaging waste, and other regulated waste through authorized systems. Site-specific approval conditions control where stricter than general standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal fire prevention approval and an occupancy permit before operations. Provide fire-alarm, sprinkler, emergency-lighting, exit, extinguisher, hazardous-material, compressed-gas, and flammable-liquid controls appropriate to the site. Obtain structural and mechanical sign-off for tanks, mezzanines, keg storage, racking, boilers, refrigeration, and loading areas; verify floor loading and anchorage by qualified professionals. Complete electrical, gas, pressure-vessel, plumbing, and ventilation inspections where applicable. Maintain Alberta OHS compliance, WHMIS records, machine guarding, lockout procedures, confined-space controls, hot-work procedures, emergency plans, and worker training.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada. The Department of Finance Canada administers federal financial-sector policy, while the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers anti-money-laundering and terrorist-financing compliance. The Canada Border Services Agency, Canada Revenue Agency, and provincial liquor authority regulate relevant trade, tax, excise, and alcohol activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada has no general exchange controls and the Canadian dollar is generally freely convertible for current-account and capital-account transactions. A Canadian corporation may generally receive, hold, convert, and remit foreign currency, dividends, interest, royalties, service fees, loan proceeds, and repayment amounts, subject to corporate-law solvency requirements, applicable withholding tax, transfer-pricing rules, thin-capitalization rules, beneficial-ownership verification, sanctions, anti-money-laundering controls, lender covenants, and documented corporate purpose. Canada does not generally require prior central-bank approval for foreign investment, capital contributions, intercompany loans, or profit repatriation. Dividend declarations by an Alberta unlimited liability corporation must comply with applicable corporate-law solvency tests and the entity's governing documents. The ULC is not automatically fiscally transparent for Canadian tax purposes; Canadian tax classification and any foreign tax treatment must be separately confirmed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no general statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds to a Canadian bank, convert export receipts into Canadian dollars, or convert a prescribed percentage of export proceeds. No general statutory conversion deadline applies. Exporters may retain proceeds in foreign-currency accounts, subject to contractual banking terms and accounting, tax, customs, sanctions, and anti-money-laundering obligations. Export transactions must be supported by commercial records, customs documentation, invoices, shipping records, and proof of delivery where relevant. Foreign-currency balances and transactions must be recorded under applicable Canadian accounting and tax rules. Banks may request transaction-purpose, beneficiary, source-of-funds, and trade-document evidence and may impose internal risk-based controls.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Alberta Treasury Branches, operating as ATB Financial
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account; Canadian-dollar accounts and selected foreign-exchange services, subject to eligibility and product approval

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium for payment initiation, foreign-exchange execution, expense management, and collection support; low as a substitute for a full Canadian operating bank. An offshore electronic-money institution generally cannot accept deposits or conduct deposit-taking in Canada without the required Canadian authorization. A foreign payment service provider may serve the corporation cross-border subject to its home-jurisdiction authorization, Canadian payment-services requirements where applicable, contractual corridor restrictions, sanctions screening, settlement-bank controls, and FINTRAC registration obligations if it conducts regulated services in Canada. Canadian payment service providers may be subject to the Retail Payment Activities Act and Bank of Canada supervision when the statutory regime applies. Offshore EMI balances may lack Canadian deposit insurance, Canadian creditor protection, and reliable access to domestic clearing. Use a Canadian bank for payroll, tax, liquor-related payments, recurring local debits, and primary liquidity; use an EMI only after confirming licensing, safeguarding, settlement, data, insolvency, and account-closure protections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No universal Canadian statutory rule requires every director to appear physically at a bank branch. Remote onboarding may be available for Canadian corporations, but acceptance is bank-specific and depends on identity-verification results, ownership complexity, foreign ownership, business risk, expected transaction corridors, and the bank's policies. Banks must identify and verify the corporation, directors, authorized signatories, beneficial owners and controlling persons under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and related regulations. A branch visit, video interview, certified copies, Canadian notarial authentication, or in-person signing may be required for foreign directors, nominee arrangements, high-risk jurisdictions, incomplete digital identity records, or unresolved ownership concerns. The corporation should maintain a Canadian registered office, Canadian tax and corporate records, a clear operating rationale, and a documented local management and delivery model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign ownership or control of an Alberta ULC with no apparent Canadian commercial substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate and articles of incorporation, Alberta corporate registry profile, corporate structure chart, register of directors and shareholders, ultimate-beneficial-owner declarations, passports and residential-address evidence for all relevant individuals, board resolutions, Canadian registered-office evidence, Alberta operating address, business plan, employment and warehouse agreements, and explanation of the ULC's commercial and tax rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between stated craft-beer distribution activity and expected international flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed customer and supplier contracts, product catalogue, brewery and distributor licenses, AGLC approvals, CRA excise documentation, import or export records, customs broker mandate, shipping lanes, invoices, purchase orders, bills of lading, cold-chain logistics agreements, expected monthly volume, currencies, counterparties, and transaction-purpose matrix.

Applicable Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis documentation, liquor licences and registrations, federal excise and alcohol-related registrations where required, CBSA import and export records, CFIA or food-safety documentation where applicable, warehouse and transportation authorizations, product-origin records, and written confirmation of the corporation's permitted wholesale, distribution, and export activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound shareholder funding or intercompany loans with unclear source of wealth or source of funds
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Subscription agreement or loan agreement, board approval, lender or shareholder ownership records, audited financial statements, bank statements, tax returns, sale-of-business or investment records, funding-flow diagram, sanctions screening, beneficial-owner identification, and a pre-advice package to the receiving bank before remittance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments involving sanctioned, restricted, or high-risk jurisdictions or counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty KYC file, ownership and control analysis, sanctions-screening results, end-use and end-user statement, shipping route, vessel and carrier details, origin and destination evidence, trade-license records, payment rationale, and legal review under Canadian sanctions administered by Global Affairs Canada.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume cash, cash-equivalent, or unusual third-party payments inconsistent with wholesale distribution
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Cashless-payment policy, customer onboarding standards, account-reconciliation reports, deposit records, invoices, delivery confirmations, credit-control procedures, refund policy, related-party analysis, and written explanation of any third-party settlement arrangement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Failure to evidence tax, customs, excise, or corporate good standing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CRA business number, GST/HST registration where applicable, corporate tax filings, Alberta corporate annual returns, municipal and provincial registrations, excise filings, customs account information, liquor compliance records, and certificates or correspondence evidencing good standing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent expected account activity, currencies, counterparties, or beneficial-owner information
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Approved treasury policy, 12-month cash-flow forecast, account-purpose schedule, currency exposure analysis, authorized-signatory matrix, related-party register, monthly transaction-volume estimates, foreign-exchange policy, and documented change-notification process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of an unlimited-liability corporation creating perceived shareholder or creditor risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta corporate-law memorandum, constitutional documents, solvency policy, director approvals, insurance schedule, capitalization plan, intercompany indemnities where appropriate, creditor-risk assessment, and explanation that the ULC's unlimited liability is a statutory corporate attribute rather than evidence of undisclosed personal banking.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route equity through a Canadian bank account in the exact legal name of the Alberta ULC. Obtain bank pre-clearance for material or foreign-originated funds. Use a wire transfer identifying the sender, beneficiary, Canadian account number, financial institution, amount, currency, and purpose such as paid-up capital, share subscription, capital contribution, or shareholder loan. Canada generally has no central-bank capital-inflow purpose-code regime; therefore, the bank's narrative, supporting documents, and internal transaction classification must be accurate and consistent. For equity, retain the subscription agreement, directors' resolution, share issuance records, capitalization table, beneficial-owner evidence, and source-of-funds file. For debt, retain the executed loan agreement, interest and maturity terms, transfer-pricing support, withholding-tax analysis, and repayment schedule. Avoid third-party funding, unexplained pass-through transfers, split payments designed to evade controls, and unsupported payments to personal accounts. Reconcile the receipt to the general ledger and preserve SWIFT or ISO 20022 payment confirmations. Foreign-exchange conversion should occur through the Canadian bank or an appropriately regulated provider, with rate, trade confirmation, and accounting records retained.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use Canadian bank domestic clearing for Canadian suppliers and customers, including EFT, Interac-enabled commercial solutions where appropriate, pre-authorized debits, and other bank-approved local rails. Use SWIFT MT103 or ISO 20022 pacs.008 for cross-border single-customer credit transfers, with complete originator, beneficiary, bank, invoice, and purpose information. Use commercial letters of credit, documentary collections, bank guarantees, or supply-chain finance where counterparty, jurisdiction, cargo, or credit risk justifies documentary control. Trade payments should match purchase orders, invoices, customs declarations, bills of lading, certificates of origin, excise and liquor documentation, and proof of delivery. Canadian banks may require sanctions screening, end-use review, dual-use analysis, and additional information for shipments or counterparties in elevated-risk jurisdictions. Payment descriptions must not mischaracterize alcohol, excise, related-party, royalty, loan, or capital transactions. For recurring local collections, implement bank-approved direct debit mandates with customer authorization, return handling, segregation of duties, and transaction monitoring. Maintain a three-way reconciliation among bank records, trade documents, and the accounts payable or receivable ledger.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD, CAD/EUR, CAD/GBP, and other bank-approved foreign-exchange forwards for documented commercial exposures, subject to counterparty credit approval and ISDA or equivalent documentation where required
Foreign-exchange spot transactions for settlement and operational conversion

Currency options, collars, and option combinations where approved by the bank, suitably documented, and consistent with the corporation's risk-management policy; avoid speculative or uncovered positions

Non-deliverable forwards for currencies or jurisdictions where physical delivery is restricted or unavailable, subject to Canadian bank approval, applicable local-law restrictions, sanctions screening, and documented underlying exposure

Cross-currency swaps and currency swaps for hedging committed intercompany or external borrowing, subject to treasury-policy limits, counterparty documentation, collateral terms, accounting treatment, and board-approved authority

Interest-rate and cross-currency hedging may require ISDA documentation, a credit-support annex, suitability assessments, confirmations, valuation controls, and periodic collateral or margin management

All hedges should be linked to identifiable forecast or committed exposures, approved under a board or management treasury policy, independently confirmed, valued periodically, reconciled to the general ledger, and reported separately from speculative trading activity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) (ABCA), filed through the Service Alberta Corporate Registry online portal, confirming registered office, current directors and principal business activity.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate Registry Branch, Service Alberta / Alberta Business Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days (2 months) after the corporation's annual incorporation-anniversary date; first annual return due in the first annual cycle following the ULC registration date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Corporation placed in overdue/inactive status and Certificate of Good Standing withheld; two consecutive years of non-filing permit the Registrar to administratively dissolve the ULC under ABCA s. 213(2); reinstatement generally available within 5 years upon filing all arrears, paying the CAD 100 registry reinstatement fee and providing name consent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting or unanimous shareholder resolution in lieu of meeting, with presentation and approval of annual financial statements by the members (ABCA s. 129 and s. 152).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders; minutes and signed resolutions retained in the corporate minute book at the Alberta registered office (no registry filing unless requested in a Corporate Registry records audit).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First AGM no later than 18 months after incorporation; each subsequent AGM no more than 15 months after the prior annual meeting; financial statements must be placed before the shareholders at every annual meeting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors failing to convene the AGM or present financial statements commit an offence under ABCA s. 251 and are liable on summary conviction to a fine of up to CAD 5,000 per director; continued default can support shareholder oppression remedies and creditor applications for record inspection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal Part I corporate tax, including Alberta corporate allocation through Schedule 5) for the ULC's Canadian tax reporting.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), corporate tax division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; balance-due remittance due on the same date; quarterly tax instalments may apply where corporate tax payable exceeds prescribed thresholds.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month of delay, capped at 12 months under Income Tax Act s. 162; interest accrues at prescribed rates; unremitted payroll/GST components may trigger director-liability assessments under s. 227.1, and gross-negligence penalties can reach 50% of misreported amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return (GST34-2) covering the 5% federal GST on Canadian wholesale sales of craft beer and zero-rated export supplies of keg and packaged product.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual filers must file within 3 months after the fiscal year-end; instalments are required on a quarterly (or monthly) basis when annual net tax exceeds CAD 3,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty under Excise Tax Act s. 280 equal to 5% of unremitted tax plus 1% per month, capped at 12 months; prescribed-rate interest applies; directors may be personally assessed for unremitted GST under Excise Tax Act s. 323.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual renewal of the Alberta liquor manufacturer-distributor licence / malt-beverage general authorization enabling wholesale distribution and export of artisanal keg and packaged craft beer (class-dependent estimated fee for a small distributor).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Gaming, Liquor and Cannabis (AGLC), Liquor Licensing Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the licence anniversary date preceding the expiry date shown on the licence; renewal application and payment submitted through the AGLC online licensing portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Expired licence immediately terminates authority to purchase, warehouse or distribute liquor; unlicensed sales after expiry are unlawful and may result in AGLC administrative penalties, licence suspension or revocation, inventory surrender orders, and refusal to reissue a licence for a defined period.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory-register audit: physical inspection and officer certification of the Register of Members, Register of Directors, share transfer records, minute book and accounting records.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Directors and shareholders; records must be maintained at the Alberta registered office (or other prescribed location in Alberta) and be available for inspection by members and creditors under ABCA s. 108 and s. 136.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed immediately before or at the AGM each year and certified in writing by an officer; registers must also be updated promptly on each share transfer or director change throughout the year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance exposes each contravening director to offence fines and court-ordered rectification or damages; absent or inaccurate registers weaken the ULC's ability to document member liability and may invalidate reliance on statutory pass-through treatment of the unlimited liability entity.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset-size threshold is imposed under the ABCA. A private, non-distributing ULC is exempt from the mandatory shareholder audit only if all shareholders execute a unanimous written resolution waiving the appointment of an auditor (ABCA s. 162). Where no waiver exists, an auditor must be appointed at the AGM. Lenders, AGLC licensing conditions and major export buyers typically require audited or reviewed financial statements as a contractual covenant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) is the default framework for a private Alberta ULC; IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I) is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises and may be elected voluntarily. Inventory, keg deposits, empty-return credits, excise duty refunds, interprovincial revenue and related-party transactions must be recognized under ASPE; CRA books-and-records rules under Income Tax Act s. 230 require retention for 6 years, with a 7-year corporate retention practice adopted for ULC liability documentation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Alberta does not require a separate annual beneficial-ownership registry filing for private provincial ULCs. Compliance is satisfied by recording every share transfer in the Register of Members upon board approval, updating the director roster and registered-office details in the annual return, and preparing an internal annual beneficial-ownership reconciliation signed by a designated director and placed in the minute book. For a ULC the member register is critical because shareholders carry unlimited liability, and creditors may rely on the registered member records when enforcing obligations.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (name, last-known address, class and series of shares, issue and transfer dates and endorsements)
Register of Directors (full name, resident address, occupation, date of election, cessation and consent)
Minute Book (AGM minutes or unanimous shareholder resolutions in lieu, board consents, articles, bylaws and unanimous shareholder agreement)
Register of Securities and Transfers (certificate numbers, counterparties, consideration and transfer approval dates)
General ledgers and source documents (invoices, excise duty schedules, keg deposit reconciliations, export bills of lading and CRA filings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180 to 650 per annum (CAD 250 to 900) for a licensed Alberta registered-office and registered-agent service provider; self-managed registered office is available at negligible cost if the ULC maintains physical premises in Alberta.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 9,000 to 27,000 (CAD 12,000 to 38,000) for a full independent audit of a private craft-beer distribution ULC; USD 3,000 to 7,000 (CAD 4,000 to 10,000) for a review engagement where the statutory audit has been validly waived.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined effective headline corporate income tax rate on active business income (15% federal Part I general rate plus 8% Alberta general corporate rate).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: For a qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporation, active business income up to the federal business limit of CAD 500,000 benefits from the federal small business deduction (9% federal rate) and the Alberta small business deduction (2% provincial rate), giving an effective 11% combined rate. No manufacturing/processing credit applies to wholesale distribution. No annual capital tax applies to a pure wholesale distribution model.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal and Alberta combined) filed via CRA Corporation Internet Filing (T2 NETFILE) using certified tax preparation software; no separate Alberta corporate return is required.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the corporation's fiscal period end; final tax payment generally due two months after fiscal year-end (three months for CCPCs eligible for the small business limit).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Alberta Business Number, fiscal period, jurisdiction of incorporation (Alberta ULC), registered office and director name/address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the ULC is a specified Canadian corporation with foreign control, indicate the country of ultimate parent and enter the address for service of process; nominate a significant presence in Alberta.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross revenue from keg sales, cost of goods sold, distribution and cold-chain logistics expenses, net income before taxes.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Translated to Canadian dollars using the Bank of Canada average annual exchange rate; file on the same basis as the audited financial statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Details of all cross-border related-party transactions: beer purchases/sales, licensing fees, management fees, loans, and intercompany service charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A separate T106 is due if the aggregate value exceeds CAD 1,000,000; the schedule identifies each non-resident affiliate, the amount and the transfer-pricing method.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta taxable income, provincial general rate 8%, small business deduction 2% on eligible active business income, provincial tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident corporation carrying on business through a permanent establishment in Alberta, allocate Alberta taxable income under the Income Tax Act regulations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties under Income Tax Act s. 162(1): 5% of the balance due plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeat offence: 10% plus 2% per month up to 20 months. Late payment interest under s. 161(1) compounds daily at the prescribed CRA rate. Failure to file the T106 information return attracts specific penalties, and gross negligence in filing can trigger a 50% civil penalty.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act, subject to reduction under an applicable tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To rely on a treaty, the non-resident payee must provide the Canadian payer with the appropriate residency certificate (e.g., US Form 6166) and a declaration that the beneficial owner is the treaty claimant. In practice, the CRA requires Form NR301 or NR302 when the payer is not exempting the payment at source; otherwise the recipient can file Form NR7-R to claim a refund of over-withheld tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest 25% and royalties 25%. Under the Canada–US convention, arm's-length interest is generally subject to 0%; industrial and patent royalties 10%; copyright and software royalties may be subject to 0% in the case of specific literary/artistic copyright.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: CAD 1,000,000 for the filing of the T106 return; a full contemporaneous transfer-pricing report is expected whenever related-party cross-border transactions occur, and CRA routinely requests it even below that threshold.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has no separate Economic Substance Regulations, but the CRA applies the GAAR and substance-over-form principles. The treaty entitlement of a ULC is ring-fenced by the OECD principal purpose test; an Alberta ULC that lacks employees, premises, inventory management and commercial planning will be recharacterised as a shell and denied treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or understatement of gross revenue from keg and cold-chain sales, fabrication of expenses, or falsification of inventory records to lower Canadian taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 50% of the understated tax under ITA s. 163(2), plus compounded daily interest; criminal liability under ITA s. 239(1) carries a fine up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director or officer who directs or participates in evasion is personally exposed to criminal fines, imprisonment, and travel restrictions; civilly, CRA may apply s. 160 to transfers of assets to non-arm's-length parties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring the Alberta ULC as an invoice-passing intermediary that lacks commercial substance, using intercompany management fees to strip profits, or filing contradictory treaty residency claims in Canada and the United States.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR applies to disregard the arrangement, reallocate income, deny treaty benefits and impose normal tax at 23% combined, with late-payment interest and penalties; administrative penalty exposure up to 50% on gross misstatement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Responsible directors may be jointly assessed for unremitted Part XIII withholding under s. 227.1 if the artificial payments were made out of the Canadian entity; they may be ordered to make restitution in CRA civil proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to develop and maintain credible customer due-diligence records for bulk cash customers, avoiding suspicious-transaction reporting for wire transfers to/from high-risk jurisdictions, and using third-party clearing accounts to settle keg sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: FINTRAC penalties: up to CAD 1,000,000 for corporations per failure; conviction for money laundering under the Criminal Code carries imprisonment up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers can be charged as parties to the offence where they actively set up or oversee compensatory anti-money-laundering bypass mechanisms; the Crown may seek forfeiture of corporate assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Misapplying the arm's length standard so that the resulting taxable-income adjustment constitutes a gross misstatement: the transfer-pricing adjustment exceeds 10% of the ULC's gross revenue and CAD 5 million, or other statutory conditions are met.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under ITA s. 247(3), a transfer-pricing penalty of 10% of the transfer-pricing adjustment is imposed; the underlying corporate tax is reduced or eliminated only if the adjustment is reversed; no offsetting deduction is available.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing inaccurate T106 certificates or knowingly approving false intercompany pricing are not personally liable for the corporation's tax debt under s. 227.1 absent s. 160 in rem arrangements, but they face criminal exposure for fraudulent tax returns and professional disciplinary action.
